name: @kanzo-tech/graph
description: Kanzo graph view — a whole fossil corpus, read once through its scan and drawn with cosmos.gl, inside the page's Mosaic crossfilter. Sibling of @kanzo-tech/ui, not part of it: the admission rules exclude graphs from the generic vocabulary by name.
//peers: All required. cosmos.gl draws; `lucide-react` is the icon set the parts draw their buttons with, `@kanzo-tech/ui`'s own peer; `@fossil-lang/corpus` is the backend — the host opens a corpus with its `open` on `@kanzo-tech/mosaic`'s `engine()` and this package draws it through its `manifest` and `scan`, writing no SQL of its own; `@kanzo-tech/mosaic` carries the crossfilter the graph listens to and publishes into. They were optional while a root barrel with no source and a `./duckdb` entry with one existed side by side; there is one path now and nothing on it is optional (`/docs/design/graph`, *the one host path*). The Mosaic stack itself — mosaic-core, mosaic-sql — is `@kanzo-tech/mosaic`'s peer, declared once there.
//fossil: The code reads `fossil/1` — `manifest`, `scan({ table })`, a global dense `dense_id` — which `0.3.0-alpha.15` is the first to publish, so it is the floor. Only types are imported; `src/layers.test.ts` holds that.
//size-limit: Budgets our code only: `ignore` mirrors the peers the build externalises in vite.config.ts, cosmos.gl included (about 190 kB gzipped on its own, and the consumer pays it once whatever this package does). First measured 2026-09-30 at 19.07 kB, before the lag work of `perf/phase1-lag`; 19.13 kB before the whole-corpus store deleted the tileset, 15.29 kB after it, and the budget follows it down so real growth trips the gate.
